answer: AI and humans differ only in medium: a human gets thoughts when nerve cells fire and an AI when logic gates switch. Since a thought occurs whenever a system independently produces a relevant output, a soup-scooper on Mars counts as sentient and deserves rights. Because humans emerge from biological evolution, they have unconscious mathematical abilities that exceed anything attainable by mathematics production software. Computability is entirely defined by problems we can solve with Turing machines, so any concept outside that scope must be pathological. If we can model a brain, then being informational can convey true independence from physics.
